chapter: Cab Calloway, Lunceford, Hampton and Armstrong, 1941-45
title: Artie Shaw gives up his band; unrecorded tunes
summary: Robbins told McRae he lost half a million dollars when Shaw quit, leaving unrecorded McRae tunes.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

No. I think I had finished with Artie, because after that Artie had broke up his band.
Hollywood where he (inaudible) broke his leg out there in the swimming pool, or something.

And then he decided he wanted to go -- you know, be an author. He wanted to write books. Jack Robbins called me up one day and say, "Look, you just lost a half a million dollars." I say, "Why?" "Your favorite boy just give up his band, Artie Shaw."
Well we had a lot of things that Artie never recorded there -- that was just laying there, you know.
Flight By Night was the other thing.
